newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sacked Lebed urges supporters to be calm.
newsitem.headline: Sacked Lebed urges supporters to be calm.

text.p: Former Russian security chief Alexander Lebed on Thursday called on his supporters to stay calm in the wake of his dramatic sacking by President Boris Yeltsin but warned of a "hot autumn" to come.

"I call on my comrades in arms, my allies and people who I probably do not know in person...Do not do anything abrupt!. We act only using constitutional means," he told a news conference in Moscow organised by Interfax news agency.

Lebed was speaking less than three hours after Yeltsin appeared on national television and signed a decree sacking him for what the Russian leader said was his lack of team spirit and naked ambition to be president.
Lebed was more ambiguous when asked what he would do if his supporters started protesting about his dismissal.

"I want to see first whether this will happen. I will make my decisions judging by the circumstances," he replied, issuing a prediction that a severe lack of funding for the armed forces would provoke a crisis later this year.

"We are heading for a very hot autumn, no doubt about it," he said, citing a letter from a group of General Staff officers in which they told the Defence Ministry to pay all salary arrears by October 25 or face the consequences.

The letter -- published by the Nezavisimaya Gazeta newspaper on Thursday -- was addressed to Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and said that keeping the armed forces "half-starved" was a deliberate act by unnamed sinister forces who wanted to ruin Russia and surrender it to the West.
"We have enough force to make these gentlemen abandon their plans," the letter said. The newspaper did not say how many officers had signed it.
"I think this (crisis) will start on October 25, as can be seen from the letter," Lebed said.

Earlier on Thursday a Yeltsin spokesman hinted that Lebed had been stoking discontent among officers in the paratroop forces, which are due to be reduced under plans for military reform. Yeltsin sacked a deputy paratroop commander for openly protesting against the reforms.
Around 11 million people voted for Lebed in the first round of June's presidential elections, in which he finished third. A recent opinion poll said he was Russia's most trusted politician.
